bandReport.notes: Band b2 = p08-p14, Q57-Q100 complete and contiguous (44 items). SEAM BEFORE: p07 (band b1's territory) was opened but NOT transcribed - it ends cleanly at Q56 with all four options printed, and NO Directions block is open across the p07/p08 boundary, so Q57 starts clean and nothing is stranded between the bands. SEAM AFTER: none - p14 is the LAST page of the booklet (p00-p14) and the paper genuinely ENDS AT Q100. Verified by cropping the foot of p14: the last printed content is Q100 option (d) '147.92 cm', followed only by the footer 'STS-M-TPT  ( 30 - A )'. NO ANSWER KEY appears anywhere on p08-p14 - no key page, no key table, no marginal answers. ONE Directions set, and it STARTS inside this band so this band owns every member: D86-90, headed 'For the next five (05) items that follow :', a PROSE caselet about 1200 university students across Mathematics/Statistics/Physics/Chemistry. Its block and Q86 are on p12; Q87-Q90 are overleaf on p13. All five members are transcribed here, contiguous, each carrying the identical verbatim context. ZERO FIGURES in this whole band - no question on p08-p14 carries a printed diagram, so hasFigure is set on none of them. Worth stating explicitly because the band is geometry-heavy (Q57-Q84) and figures normally cluster in the last pages of these booklets: every geometry stem here states its configuration entirely in words. The one near-miss is Q94, whose stem talks about 'the pie diagrams on the monthly expenditure of two families A and B' - but NO pie chart is printed; the question asks which underlying data would produce radii in the ratio 16:9, so it is fully answerable from the text. That is recorded as a flag on Q94 rather than as a figure. RUPEE GLYPH: the booklet prints the Unicode rupee sign in Q92 and in all four options of Q94 (confirmed at 3x zoom - it is the modern rupee sign, not 'Rs.'). Transcribed as 'Rs.' per the brief's currency rule and to match the shipped corpus, where 'Rs.' occurs 282 times across the sibling band files and the rupee sign occurs zero times. The value is unchanged. DECIMALS: the booklet sets a raised middle dot throughout (0.5 cm in Q57, 12.5 / 9.375 in Q64, 9.5 in Q66, 1.25 / 6.25 in Q76, 2.25 / 4.5 in Q77, 58.8 / 73.5 / 78.7 / 80.6 in Q87, 4.4 / 4.5 / 5.0 / 2.5 in Q93, 144.32 / 145.52 / 146.72 / 147.92 in Q100); all transcribed as full stops per the brief. TWO INVENTED SUBTOPICS, both flagged on the questions themselves: 'Counting Intersection Points of Lines' (Q83 - a counting/combinatorics item, and the catalog has no permutations-and-combinations chapter) and 'Caselet Data Interpretation' (Q86-Q90 - the shared stimulus is prose, so none of Data Interpretation's three subtopics (Tables / Bar and Line Graphs / Pie Charts) fits). ONE MISPRINT-ish item flagged: Q76's options are pure multiples of pi-squared with no unit, while the quantity asked for is a volume - transcribed exactly as printed, not repaired. Two classifications follow shipped sibling precedent rather than my first instinct: Q98 (primary vs secondary data) -> Statistics / Frequency Distributions and Classification, matching 2019-2 Q66; Q97 (geometric mean) -> Sequence and Series / Harmonic Progressions and the Three Means, matching 2018-1 Q52, 2020-2 Q100 and 2022-1 Q30. Ambiguous glyphs were cropped and re-read at 3-5x rather than guessed: Q61's option denominators (8 vs 16), Q64's 12.5 / 9.375, Q68's option (c), Q74's 60pi, Q75's 87500 / 26500, Q90's option (d) 189:179, Q92's rupee sign, Q94's amounts, and Q97's square root vs cube root. Nothing in this band was left unreadable.
